applied_text: test_that("D-optimal projection P is the hat matrix of [1, X] when a covariate is an affine shift of another", {
evidence: DesignFixedGreedyDOptimal$draw_ws_according_to_design -> private$draw_ws_raw (R/EDI/R/design_fixed_greedy_d_optimal.R:303 ensure_model_matrix_current; create_model_matrix_from_features drops dependent columns only among X without the intercept, R/EDI/R/helper_model_matrix.R:83-84, so [x1, x1+1] keeps rank 2) -> build_optimal_design_P_H (design_fixed_greedy_d_optimal.R:325) -> Z0 = cbind(1, X); Z0_qr = qr(Z0); Q = qr.Q(Z0_qr); P = Q %*% t(Q) (R/EDI/R/helper_optimal_shared.R:106-110) uses all ncol(Z0) columns of Q even though Z0_qr$rank = 2 -> d_optimal_search_cpp(P, ...) (design_fixed_greedy_d_optimal.R:338). The same helper feeds DesignFixedOptimal::build_solver_inputs (R/EDI/R/design_fixed_optimal.R:459). The need_H branch (helper_optimal_shared.R:112-113) has the same rank-deficient R.
fix_hint: Keep only the first Z0_qr$rank columns of qr.Q (P = Q[, seq_len(Z0_qr$rank)] %*% t(...)), or drop the pivoted-out columns of Z0 before building P and H.
test_code:
set.seed(1)
	n = 30L
	x1 = rnorm(n)
	X = data.frame(x1 = x1, x2 = x1 + 1)
	des = DesignFixedGreedyDOptimal$new(response_type = "continuous", n = n, verbose = FALSE, seed = 1L)
	des$add_all_subjects_to_experiment(X)
	W = des$draw_ws_according_to_design(r = 2L)
	expect_equal(dim(W), c(n, 2L))
	P = des$.__enclos_env__$private$P
	Z0 = cbind(1, x1)
	P_true = Z0 %*% solve(crossprod(Z0)) %*% t(Z0)
	expect_equal(sum(diag(P)), 2, tolerance = 1e-8)
	expect_equal(unname(P), unname(P_true), tolerance = 1e-8)
test_name: D-optimal projection P is the hat matrix of [1, X] when a covariate is an affine shift of another
text: When the covariates are linearly independent but become collinear once the intercept is added (e.g. x2 = x1 + 1, or two 0/1 indicators that sum to 1), the non-Bayesian criterion matrix is built as P = Q Q' from qr.Q(qr(cbind(1, X))) without truncating to the QR rank. P then projects onto a rank(Z0)+1 dimensional space that includes an arbitrary Householder direction, rather than onto col(Z0). The D/A search therefore optimizes the wrong criterion: trace(P) is 3 instead of 2 for X = [x1, x1 + 1].

applied_text: test_that("KK21 stepwise design keeps assigning with finite weights when all count responses so far are zero", {
evidence: DesignSeqOneByOneKK21stepwise inherits assign_wt from DesignSeqOneByOneKK21 (design_seq_one_by_one_KK21_stepwise.R:85). design_seq_one_by_one_KK21.R:263 calls private$compute_weights, which for count with the speedup goes to design_seq_one_by_one_KK21_stepwise.R:269, na0(kk21_stepwise_continuous_weights_cpp(xs, log(ys + 1), ws)). In src/kk21_weights.cpp:204-233 a constant y gives c = 0, so sse = 0 and sigma2 = 0, every candidate is skipped (continue), and best_j < 0 breaks at :246, leaving weights all NA (:173). na0 turns these into all 0, which passes the assert at KK21.R:265. KK21.R:270 computes raw_weights / sum(raw_weights) = NaN. compute_weighted_sqd_distances_cpp (KK21.R:295) and the bootstrap distances (KK21.R:310) are then NaN, and stats::quantile at KK21.R:316 errors with 'missing values and NaN's not allowed'.
fix_hint: In assign_wt, when sum(raw_weights) is 0 or not finite, fall back to equal weights or to super$assign_wt() (KK14) instead of dividing by zero.
test_name: KK21 stepwise design keeps assigning with finite weights when all count responses so far are zero
text: When every response collected so far is identical (e.g. a count trial whose first responses are all 0, so log(y + 1) is constant), kk21_stepwise_continuous_weights_cpp finds sigma2 = 0 for every candidate and returns all NA. na0() turns these into all-zero raw weights. KK21's assign_wt then normalizes them as 0/0 = NaN, so the weighted distances are NaN and the next assignment errors in stats::quantile (or leaves NaN covariate weights).

applied_text: test_that("KK21 proportion speedup weights stay informative when a response is exactly 1", {
evidence: The assert at design_abstract.R:1058 accepts proportion y in the closed interval [0, 1]. assign_wt (KK21.R:263) calls compute_weights, which at KK21.R:380 calls kk21_continuous_weights_cpp(xs, log(ys/(1-ys))). In src/kk21_weights.cpp:33-37, sumy and sumy2 become Inf, so b1, b0 and sse are Inf or NaN, and se_b1 is non-finite. The weight is set to eps at :70-71 for every j. The normalized covariate weights become uniform, discarding the outcome signal.
fix_hint: Clamp ys to [eps, 1 - eps] (as the stepwise subclass does) or apply a Smithson-Verkuilen squeeze before taking the logit at KK21.R:380.
test_code:
set.seed(5)
	des = DesignSeqOneByOneKK21$new(n = 30, response_type = "proportion", verbose = FALSE)
	for (i in 1 : 25){
		x1 = rnorm(1)
		des$add_one_subject_to_experiment_and_assign(data.frame(x1 = x1, x2 = rnorm(1)))
		y = if (i == 3) 1 else stats::plogis(1.5 * x1 + rnorm(1, sd = 0.2))
		des$add_one_subject_response(i, y)
	}
	priv = des$.__enclos_env__$private
	priv$all_subject_data_cache = list()
	asd = priv$compute_all_subject_data()
	w_out = priv$compute_weights(asd)
	expect_true(all(is.finite(w_out)))
	expect_true(max(w_out) > 1e-6)
test_name: KK21 proportion speedup weights stay informative when a response is exactly 1
text: With proportion_use_speedup = TRUE (the default), compute_weights passes log(ys / (1 - ys)) to the kernel without clamping. A single valid proportion response of exactly 0 or 1 becomes -Inf or +Inf, which makes every per-covariate t-statistic NaN or Inf. The kernel then returns machine epsilon for every covariate, so all outcome information is silently lost and matching becomes unweighted. The stepwise subclass clamps 0 and 1 for exactly this case (KK21_stepwise.R:272-274).

applied_text: test_that("ratio annealing never returns an infeasible allocation with a non-positive denominator", {
evidence: optimal_solve_auto (helper_optimal_annealing.R:171) / annealing_solve_A_ratio (helper_optimal_annealing.R:84) -> annealing_solve_kernel (helper_optimal_annealing.R:48) -> annealing_design_search_cpp: init_state (design_optimal_annealing_search.cpp:99-126) draws a random BCRD start with no feasibility check -> f_cur = state_objective (cpp:178, formula at cpp:77) divides by n_T - quad_P, which can be <= 0 -> chain_best_f = f_cur (cpp:180). Later moves into infeasible states are rejected (cpp:206), but the infeasible start was already recorded as the best -> exact_objective (cpp:93) recomputes the same negative ratio -> argmin over chains (cpp:247) picks it -> the R wrapper returns res$w/res$objective_value unchecked (helper_optimal_annealing.R:54-56).
fix_hint: In the ratio kernel, treat a state with n_T - w'Pw <= 1e-12 as objective +Inf in state_objective/exact_objective (or redraw the start until it is feasible), so an infeasible start can never be recorded as a chain's best.
test_code:
set.seed(1)
	n = 10L
	n_T = 5L
	# w'Pw = 2.5 + k, where k = number treated among units 1..5: allocations with
	# k <= 2 are feasible (n_T - w'Pw > 0); k >= 3 makes the denominator negative.
	P = diag(c(rep(1.5, 5), rep(0.5, 5)))
	H = matrix(0, n, n)
	res = EDI:::annealing_solve_A_ratio(P, H, n_T, n_chains = 8L, max_iter = 500L)
	w = as.numeric(res$w)
	expect_equal(sum(w), n_T)
	den = n_T - drop(t(w) %*% P %*% w)
	expect_gt(den, 0)
	expect_gt(res$objective_value, 0)
test_name: ratio annealing never returns an infeasible allocation with a non-positive denominator
text: For the A-optimal "ratio" objective, the annealing kernel scores each chain's random starting allocation as (w'Hw+1)/(n_T-w'Pw) without checking that the denominator is positive. A start with n_T-w'Pw <= 0 (or a denominator that is ~0 but slightly negative from rounding, as when w lies in the column span of the design so w'Pw = n_T) gets a negative or -huge objective. That value becomes the chain's best and beats every feasible allocation. annealing_solve_A_ratio then returns an infeasible allocation with a negative objective_value, even though its own f_exact (helper_optimal_annealing.R:88) scores that allocation as Inf.

applied_text: test_that("mahal_dist objective is not dropped for a full-rank but badly scaled covariate matrix", {
evidence: DesignFixedOptimal builds its objective inputs at R/EDI/R/design_fixed_optimal.R:478 with prepare_optimal_objective_matrices(X, obj), where X is the raw covariate matrix (design_fixed_optimal.R:501). In R/EDI/R/helper_optimal_milp_solvers.R:102, Sigma = crossprod(Xc)/(n-1) has diagonal of about (1e-14, 1). rcond(Sigma) is about 1e-14, below 1e-12, so line 106 sets ch = NULL. Lines 111-116 then return kind = 'l1' with mahal_fell_back = TRUE. The greedy kernel (src/design_fixed_greedy.cpp:119-123) uses LLT, which succeeds on this Sigma, so the MILP path optimizes a different criterion than the greedy kernel it claims to match.
fix_hint: Run the singularity check on the correlation matrix (Sigma scaled by its diagonal), or try chol() with pivot = TRUE and check its rank, so that rescaling a column cannot turn mahal_dist into the l1 fallback.
test_code:
set.seed(1)
	n = 12
	X_raw = cbind(x1 = rnorm(n) * 1e-7, x2 = rnorm(n))
	prep = EDI:::prepare_optimal_objective_matrices(X_raw, "mahal_dist")
	expect_identical(prep$kind, "quadratic")
	expect_false(isTRUE(prep$mahal_fell_back))
	# Mahalanobis is invariant to column scaling: reference from standardized columns
	Xs = scale(X_raw, center = TRUE, scale = TRUE)
	Ss = crossprod(Xs) / (n - 1)
	Q_ref = 4 * Xs %*% solve(Ss) %*% t(Xs) / n^2
	w = c(rep(1, 6), rep(0, 6))
	f_ref = drop(t(w) %*% Q_ref %*% w)
	f_got = if (identical(prep$kind, "quadratic")) drop(t(w) %*% prep$Q %*% w) else NA_real_
	expect_equal(f_got, f_ref, tolerance = 1e-8)
test_name: mahal_dist objective is not dropped for a full-rank but badly scaled covariate matrix
text: prepare_optimal_objective_matrices() decides whether Sigma is singular with rcond(Sigma) < 1e-12. rcond is not invariant to column scaling, so a full-rank covariate matrix whose columns are on very different scales (for example one covariate around 1e-7 and another around 1) is treated as singular. The function then silently drops mahal_dist and uses the abs_sum_diff l1 objective (mahal_fell_back = TRUE). The Mahalanobis objective is scale-invariant and well defined here, and the greedy kernel's Eigen LLT succeeds on the same Sigma.

applied_text: test_that("CR2 cluster-robust variance is scale-equivariant for responses in small units", {
evidence: InferenceContinuousOLS private$shared() (R/EDI/R/inference_continuous_ols.R:420) -> apply_cluster_robust_se (inference_continuous_ols.R:399) -> cluster_robust_cr2_variance (helper_robust_sandwich.R:116) -> `if (!is.finite(ssq) || ssq < .Machine$double.eps) return(NULL)` (helper_robust_sandwich.R:155) -> apply_cluster_robust_se returns FALSE at inference_continuous_ols.R:400 and the non-clustered SE stays in place. Lin uses the same path (inference_continuous_lin.R:392).
fix_hint: Make the degeneracy floor relative to the data scale, e.g. compare ssq against .Machine$double.eps * (sum(e^2) or var(y)) * XtX_inv[j, j], not against an absolute constant.
test_code:
set.seed(1)
	n = 60
	cluster = rep(1:6, each = 10)
	w = rep(c(0, 1), 30)
	x = rnorm(n)
	X = cbind(1, w, x)
	y = 1 + 0.5 * w + 0.3 * x + rnorm(6)[cluster] + rnorm(n)
	coef_hat = as.numeric(qr.coef(qr(X), y))
	cr = EDI:::cluster_robust_cr2_variance(X, y, coef_hat, cluster, 2L)
	expect_false(is.null(cr))
	s = 1e-8
	cr_small = EDI:::cluster_robust_cr2_variance(X, y * s, coef_hat * s, cluster, 2L)
	expect_false(is.null(cr_small))
	if (!is.null(cr_small)) {
		expect_equal(cr_small$ssq, cr$ssq * s^2, tolerance = 1e-6)
		expect_equal(cr_small$df, cr$df, tolerance = 1e-6)
	}
test_name: CR2 cluster-robust variance is scale-equivariant for responses in small units
text: cluster_robust_cr2_variance() returns NULL whenever the CR2 variance is below the absolute floor .Machine$double.eps, so a continuous response measured in small units (e.g. y * 1e-8) is declared not estimable. The CR2 variance is well defined and scales exactly with y^2. When the result is NULL, InferenceContinuousOLS / Lin silently keep the homoskedastic independent-subjects SE on a cluster design instead of the cluster-robust one.

applied_text: test_that("Breslow cumulative hazard is exact when late risk sets have very low relative risk", {
evidence: .cox_simulate_stratified (helper_survival_fits.R:614) / Cox null simulation callers -> .breslow_hazard (helper_survival_fits.R:582): risk = exp(eta - max(eta)) (line 585), R_k = sum(risk_o[at_risk]) (line 594), h_acc = h_acc + d_k / max(R_k, 1e-10) (line 596). The floor applies to the max-rescaled quantity, so it bites whenever the at-risk linear predictors are far below the global max, not only when R_k underflows to 0.
fix_hint: Only guard an exact underflow (R_k == 0), or accumulate the increments on the log scale with a per-risk-set log-sum-exp instead of flooring the rescaled sum at an absolute 1e-10.
test_code:
y = c(1, 2, 3)
	dead = c(1, 1, 1)
	X = matrix(c(30, 0, 0), ncol = 1)
	b_null = 1
	bh = EDI:::.breslow_hazard(y, dead, X, b_null)
	risk = exp(as.numeric(X %*% b_null) - 30)
	ref = cumsum(c(1 / sum(risk), 1 / sum(risk[2:3]), 1 / risk[3]))
	expect_equal(bh$times, c(1, 2, 3))
	expect_equal(bh$cumhaz, ref, tolerance = 1e-8)
test_name: Breslow cumulative hazard is exact when late risk sets have very low relative risk
text: .breslow_hazard() rescales risks by exp(eta - max(eta)) and then floors each risk-set sum at an absolute 1e-10. When the risk set at a later event time contains only subjects whose linear predictor is more than about 23 below the maximum, the true sum (e.g. 2*exp(-30) = 1.9e-13) is replaced by 1e-10. The cumulative baseline-hazard increment is then wrong by orders of magnitude (1e10 instead of 5.3e12), so Cox simulations that invert this hazard draw the wrong survival times.

evidence: InferenceSurvivalLogRank$compute_asymp_two_sided_pval (R/EDI/R/inference_survival_log_rank.R:153) -> private$invert_ci_to_find_two_sided_pval_for_treatment_effect (R/EDI/R/inference_all_abstract_asymp.R:201). target_fn (line 221) calls compute_asymp_confidence_interval -> compute_z_or_t_ci_from_s_and_df (line 173; df is NULL, so it uses the normal quantile). For large |z| both ends of the bracket have the same sign (line 241), so line 244 returns lower = .Machine$double.eps. Otherwise uniroot(tol = 1e-6) at line 247 returns alpha with only 1e-6 absolute accuracy. The CI is est +/- qnorm(1-alpha/2)*se, so the exact inverse is 2*pnorm(-|est-delta|/se).
fix_hint: Compute the p-value in closed form, 2*pnorm(-|est - delta|/se) (or pt with finite df), from the cached estimate and SE instead of running a root search over alpha on the CI.
status_note: test did not fail as claimed
test_code:
set.seed(1)
	n = 200
	des = DesignSeqOneByOneBernoulli$new(n = n, response_type = "survival", verbose = FALSE)
	for (i in seq_len(n)) {
		des$add_one_subject_to_experiment_and_assign(data.frame(x1 = i / 10))
	}
	w = rep(c(0, 1), length.out = n)
	des$overwrite_all_subject_assignments(w)
	y = numeric(n)
	y[w == 1] = seq_len(sum(w == 1))
	y[w == 0] = sum(w == 1) + seq_len(sum(w == 0))
	des$add_all_subject_responses(y, rep(NA_real_, n), rep(NA_real_, n))
	inf = InferenceSurvivalLogRank$new(des, verbose = FALSE)
	est = as.numeric(inf$compute_estimate())
	ci = inf$compute_asymp_confidence_interval(alpha = 0.05)
	se = as.numeric((ci[2] - ci[1]) / (2 * stats::qnorm(0.975)))
	z = est / se
	expect_true(is.finite(z) && abs(z) > 9)
	pval = inf$compute_asymp_two_sided_pval(delta = 0)
	expect_equal(as.numeric(pval), 2 * stats::pnorm(-abs(z)), tolerance = 1e-3)
test_name: log-rank Wald p-value from CI inversion matches the closed-form normal p-value for a large z
text: invert_ci_to_find_two_sided_pval_for_treatment_effect gets the Wald p-value by running uniroot over alpha on the Wald CI. The search is bounded below at .Machine$double.eps and uses an absolute tolerance of 1e-6. When |est - delta|/se > qnorm(1 - eps/2) (about 8.2), it returns exactly 2.2e-16 instead of the closed form 2*pnorm(-|z|), for example about 1e-40. Smaller p-values are only accurate to about 1e-6 in absolute terms.

	des$add_all_subjects_to_experiment(data.frame(x = rnorm(n)))

		mc_enable = TRUE,

text: With sequential Monte Carlo enabled and mc_batch_size below 10 (a positive count that normalize_randomization_ci_search_control accepts), the first batch's prefix has fewer than the 10 finite draws that compute_two_sided_randomization_pval_from_t0s requires. applied_text: test_that("Hodges-Lehmann estimate is returned when each arm is constant", {
evidence: InferenceAllSimpleWilcox$compute_estimate() (inference_all_simple_wilcox.R:56-58) -> private$shared(estimate_only = FALSE) (:302) -> stats::wilcox.test(yT, yC, conf.int = TRUE, exact = FALSE) (:330-336). This errors because at mumin = min(yT) - max(yC) every shifted observation is tied, so SIGMA.CI == 0. The error handler returns NULL -> cache_nonestimable_estimate('wilcox_fit_unavailable') (:337-339; inference_all_abstract.R:932-933 sets beta_hat_T = NA). hl_point_estimate() (:341) is never reached.
fix_hint: In shared(), compute beta via hl_point_estimate() before calling wilcox.test and cache it even when wilcox.test fails; only mark the SE/CI as non-estimable (e.g. via cache_nonestimable_se) instead of the estimate.
test_code:
set.seed(1)
	n = 20L
	des = DesignFixedBernoulli$new(response_type = "continuous", n = n, seed = 1L, verbose = FALSE)
	des$add_all_subjects_to_experiment(data.frame(x1 = rnorm(n)))
	des$assign_w_to_all_subjects()
	w = des$get_w()
	expect_true(any(w == 1) && any(w == 0))
	des$add_all_subject_responses(ifelse(w == 1, 2, 1))
	inf = InferenceAllSimpleWilcox$new(des, verbose = FALSE)

	expect_equal(inf$compute_estimate(), 1)
test_name: Hodges-Lehmann estimate is returned when each arm is constant
text: When each arm is constant (e.g. every treated y = 2 and every control y = 1), stats::wilcox.test(conf.int = TRUE) stops with 'cannot compute confidence interval when all observations are tied'. shared() catches the error and calls cache_nonestimable_estimate("wilcox_fit_unavailable"), so compute_estimate() returns NA. The Hodges-Lehmann estimate is still defined (here it is 1), and the estimate_only path returns it correctly.

applied_text: test_that("LMM null simulation uses log_sigma_e for the residual SD and log_sigma_b for the random intercept", {
evidence: ParametricLikelihoodBootstrap -> private$simulate_under_lik_null(spec, delta, null_fit) (inference_continuous_KK_glmm.R:497). It sets sigma_u = exp(b_all[p + 1L]) and sigma_e = exp(b_all[p + 2L]) (:503-504), but the kernel names b[p+1] 'log_sigma_e' and b[p+2] 'log_sigma_b' (fast_gaussian_lmm.cpp:544-545). The same class reads them in that order elsewhere: cached_vc_params passed as log_sigma_e = [1], log_sigma_b = [2] (:289-294, :333). y_sim = rnorm(n, X b + u_g, sigma_e) (:509-511) then uses the swapped SDs.
fix_hint: Swap the indices in simulate_under_lik_null: sigma_e = exp(b_all[p + 1L]) and sigma_u = exp(b_all[p + 2L]), matching the kernel's c(beta, log_sigma_e, log_sigma_b) order.
test_code:
set.seed(2)
	np = 40L
	ns = 10L
	n = 2L * np + ns
	des = DesignSeqOneByOneKK14$new(n = n, response_type = "continuous", verbose = FALSE)
	Xd = data.frame(x1 = rnorm(n))
	for (i in seq_len(n)) des$add_one_subject_to_experiment_and_assign(Xd[i, , drop = FALSE])
	des$.__enclos_env__$private$m = c(rep(seq_len(np), each = 2L), rep(0L, ns))
	w = des$get_w()
	g = c(rep(seq_len(np), each = 2L), np + seq_len(ns))
	des$add_all_subject_responses(1 + 0.5 * w + rnorm(max(g), 0, 1)[g] + rnorm(n, 0, 1))
	inf = InferenceContinKKGLMM$new(des, verbose = FALSE)
	p = inf$.__enclos_env__$private
	X = cbind(b0 = 1, w = w, x1 = Xd$x1)
	spec = list(X = X, group_id = as.integer(g), j = 2L)
	# kernel order: c(beta, log_sigma_e, log_sigma_b); sigma_e = 1, sigma_b = 3
	null_fit = list(b = c(1, 0, 0, log(1), log(3)))
	set.seed(11)
	sim = p$simulate_under_lik_null(spec, 0, null_fit)
	expect_false(is.null(sim))
	if (!is.null(sim)) {
		y_sim = environment(sim$fit_null)$y_sim
		# within a pair the mean and random intercept cancel, so var(diff) = 2 * sigma_e^2
		d = y_sim[seq(1L, 2L * np, by = 2L)] - y_sim[seq(2L, 2L * np, by = 2L)]
		sigma_e_hat = sqrt(mean(d^2) / 2)
		expect_lt(sigma_e_hat, 1.6)
		expect_gt(sigma_e_hat, 0.6)
	}

text: get_bartlett_factor_exact() computes the exact F(1, n-p) tail probability on the linear scale and returns NULL when it underflows to 0 (`p_exact <= 0`). test_name: Poisson estimate matches glm for large counts under the default zero cold start
text: With large but valid counts (cell means around 2e4) and the class's default zero cold start, the first IRLS step from beta = 0 overshoots by a factor of about 1e4. Ten step-halvings (smallest factor 2^-9) cannot bring eta below about 39, so every trial is rejected and the kernel stops at b = 0 with converged = FALSE. InferenceCountPoisson's fit_ok never checks converged, so compute_estimate() returns 0 instead of the glm MLE log(2) ~ 0.69, and the Wald SE is evaluated at b = 0.

text: zero_augmented_fit_is_degenerate() flags any fit whose first parameter (the count-model intercept) is below -15. That intercept depends on where the covariates are located, not on whether the fit is degenerate. A well-identified ZIP fit with an uncentered covariate (x1 around 80, true intercept -20, every lambda between about 0.1 and 60) is therefore treated as degenerate. The sandwich vcov returns NULL, and the marginal-estimand SE, CI and p-value come back NA. The same data with x1 centered give a finite CI, and the marginal estimand does not depend on centering.

evidence: Any host splicing InferenceMixinOffOptimumLikelihoodEval$private calls private$evaluate_penalized_neg_loglik_at(theta) (inference_mixin_off_optimum_likelihood_eval.R:92) -> evaluate_information_at returns spec$information_at(theta, source) (line 82) -> line 99 as.numeric(determinant(information, logarithm = TRUE)$modulus) ignores $sign -> line 102 checks only is.finite(log_det) -> line 105 returns the finite neg_loglik - 0.5 * log_det for a non-positive-definite information matrix.

mixin = EDI:::InferenceMixinOffOptimumLikelihoodEval
	env = new.env(parent = asNamespace("EDI"))
	priv = lapply(mixin$private, function(f) {
		environment(f) = env
		f
	})
	env$private = priv
	env$self = structure(list(), class = "FakeOffOptimumHost")
	spec = list(
		neg_loglik_at = function(theta) sum(theta^2),
		information_at = function(theta, source = "observed") diag(c(2, -3))
	)
	val = priv$evaluate_penalized_neg_loglik_at(c(0.5, 0.5), spec = spec, source = "observed")
	# log|I| is undefined for an indefinite information matrix (det = -6);
	# the documented contract is to return Inf for an infeasible penalty.
	expect_equal(val, Inf)
test_name: penalized neg-loglik is infeasible (Inf) when the information matrix is indefinite
text: evaluate_penalized_neg_loglik_at() takes determinant(...)$modulus, which is log|det I| and drops the sign. An indefinite information matrix (common for observed information away from the MLE, e.g. diag(2, -3)) has a negative determinant, so the Jeffreys/Firth penalty log|I(theta)| is undefined there. The function still returns a finite penalized objective (neg_loglik - 0.5*log 6) instead of the documented infeasibility value Inf, so an optimizer can be steered into regions where the information is not positive definite.
